note_tweet.text:
For a long time, AI or Super Intelligence, mostly meant asking a question and getting an answer. Platforms now have agents that work quietly in the background, around the clock.
Connecting your email and calendar for the first time can feel a little nerve-racking. But the more they're used, the more natural it becomes. The time and mental load you get back quickly outweigh the initial caution.
Think of it as a digital executive assistant who never sleeps and can oversee a small team of specialists. One handles research, another watches your inbox and calendar, another works on longer projects. They check in when something needs you.
Start with whichever platform fits how you already work. Grok Bots are a practical place to begin. Here’s a quick look at what’s available:
xAI – Grok Bots: Multi-bot coordination for real workflows
OpenAI – Dots: Always-on agents that connect to thousands of apps
Meta – Muse: Everyday tasks, shopping, and bookings
Anthropic – Claude Duet: Proactive help with inbox, calendar, and documents
Google – Gemini Spark: Works across Gmail, Docs, and Calendar
Choose the one that feels right and start there. Confidence builds faster than you’d think.

I'm fed up with ChatGPT. I hate that that's the case, but it's where I am.

I'm fed up with my Dot
- Losing connection to its own products, Sites, Spaces
- Refusing to create a GitHub issue because it can't find a label despite having given it permission to create labels

I'm fed up with the Desktop app
- Coming to a halt every few hours because it's consuming all my RAM, just because it's open not doing any work
- Trying to do more than it needs to, it's just too bloated

I'm sad that
- I'm getting superior results from Opus 5.5 for design and coding, even though I much prefer working with Luna, Sol and Astra
- We just never know what's going to be fixed, or when.
- Parts of OpenAI's software regularly stop working without warning, giving the impression that quality control is an afterthought

I'm just tired of fighting to make what should be simple tasks work.

I've invested an enormous amount of time building my workflows around OpenAI's ecosystem because I genuinely believe in what it's trying to achieve. That's what makes this so frustrating.
